# Solution Concept & Originality

Advising on mobility subscriptions requires recommendations to be numerically reliable and understandable without requiring the customer to inspect the underlying 
calculations. We divide these responsibilities across a hybrid architecture. Deterministic pricing and scoring engines calculate all financial and environmental 
figures. Two narrowly scoped LLM steps interpret calendar information and assess whether switching transport modes is feasible, while a single LangGraph Advisor 
handles the conversation, tariff retrieval, and what-if requests. FastAPI connects these capabilities to the frontend, PostgreSQL stores domain data, analysis snapshots, 
and agent state, and optional Langfuse tracing supports observation and evaluation of the model calls. Chapter 3 describes how these components interact.

Our contribution lies in combining multi-provider travel history, a structured subscription catalogue, calendar information, and customer priorities in one 
mobility portfolio analysis. The system compares plans within each transport category and may also recommend a shift between modes based on cost, CO~2~, and 
flexibility. The Advisor can explain the results using a curated tariff knowledge base and simulate a proposed change before asking the customer to confirm it. 
In the current prototype, a confirmed revision is saved within the application rather than executed as a real contract change with an external provider.

The brief's advanced tier suggested separate LLM agents for analysis, forecasting, optimisation, and communication. Instead of assigning every task to an agent, 
we considered where language-model reasoning added value. Analysis and optimisation became primarily deterministic components, forecasting was reduced to a 
bounded LLM step with a deterministic fallback, and only communication remained an autonomous agent. This avoids making numerical reliability depend on 
an open-ended conversation while retaining flexibility where customers need it. The deterministic output also provides a stable reference for the 
single-LLM-call baseline evaluated in Chapter 6.
